title: Voluntary-Commitment Drift x No-Versioning: Tracking Silent Walk-Backs in Frontier Safety Policies

original_idea.body:
# Voluntary-Commitment Drift x No-Versioning: Tracking Silent Walk-Backs in Frontier Safety Policies

**Problem:** Failure mode A: safety commitments are voluntary and editable. Failure mode B: there is no canonical version history, so weakened wording is invisible. Together, a lab can quietly relax a commitment (e.g. raising a capability threshold) with no governance signal — a compound erosion of accountability.

**Direction:** Use the Wayback Machine and METR's 'Common Elements' framework to diff successive versions of 4-6 labs' published frontier-safety/responsible-scaling policies over time. Code each change as strengthening/weakening/neutral against a fixed rubric, and chart the net drift. Surface specific silent walk-backs with before/after quotes.

**Why it matters:** Creates a reproducible commitment-drift monitor — the kind of independent watchdog infrastructure the ecosystem lacks. Purely archival + light NLP; high counterfactual value and a strong blog narrative.

**Relevant context:** METR Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies (metr.org/common-elements); MIRI governance agenda on enforceability gaps (intelligence.org 2025).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (detecting walk-backs aids accountability) but impact on catastrophic risk runs through accountability pressure.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused drift-monitor deliverable, some manual cross-version effort.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public archives; watchdog infra labs won't build on themselves.

low_compute.reasoning: Archival analysis plus light NLP, no compute.

novelty.reasoning: Commitment tracking exists; the version-diff drift-classification angle may be partly open; overlaps gen-903.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Commitment tracking exists but version-diff drift classification may be partly open.
